screens.screen: menu-bar popover (search field, clipboard history rows with source badge, pin and ⌘1-⌘9 shortcut badges, footer: clear all / settings / quit) on a neutral desktop

notes: SwiftUI macOS app (store name EasyCopyPaste, bundle com.somow.copypaste). Not found on this machine any more (only its landing page under somow-project/copypaste and signing files); the source was read from the private GitHub repo alfehaid/CopyPaste, shallow-cloned read-only into $W/repos/copypaste. Redrawn, not a live screenshot: NSPopover 360x480 exactly as in the code (header 12/10 padding, rows 10/6 padding with 28pt icon tile, 13pt title, 10pt source badge, 9pt monospaced ⌘n badge, selected row = accent 14%, pinned = orange pin.fill, footer), anchored under the status item whose icon is the code's SF Symbol doc.on.clipboard. All icons are the real SF Symbols named in the code, exported locally with NSImage(systemSymbolName:) into sf/*.png. Arabic localisation is used (the app ships ar + en; strings from ar.lproj), so the menu bar is mirrored as on an Arabic macOS: clock and status item on the left. Light appearance. Sample data only: the nine clipboard items and their source-app names are invented neutral snippets (hex colour, shell commands, example.com URL/email, two Arabic sentences, one image thumbnail drawn as a gradient). Source badges use the code's own fallback glyph (SF Symbol 'app') instead of real application icons, to avoid showing other apps' icons; in the running app the real app icon appears there. Desktop backdrop and menu bar are a neutral stand-in (no Apple logo, no other status items). Popover chrome (corner radius, arrow, material tint) is approximated from standard NSPopover appearance, not measured.
